chunks: As for man, whenever his Lord tries him and then is gracious and provides good things for him, he says: 'My Lord has been gracious to me.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about human nature when they are blessed with wealth and ease?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as describing the 'human' (al-insan) in his incomplete state, where prosperity leads to a sense of self-sufficiency and forgetfulness of the preceding trial. Scholars note that this psychological shift from humility in hardship to arrogance in ease serves as a precursor to the subsequent verse, where the same individual attributes the ease to his own merit, illustrating the fragility of unreflective faith.
